text:
Maya: Quick triage - VectorSherpa bring-up. Float32 baseline looks fine but PTQ 6-bit per-tensor shows ~9% drop in recall@10 on our short-query slice. Pushing notes and a minimal repro below.
Jun: ouch. Which dataset/slice was used? short queries = <=8 tokens?
Maya: yes, short_seq_holdout (<=8 tokens). Eval command I ran: 
```bash
./eval_embeddings --model vector_sherpa/fp32 --dataset short_seq_holdout --metric recall@10 > baseline.txt
./eval_embeddings --model vector_sherpa/ptq6 --dataset short_seq_holdout --metric recall@10 > ptq6.txt
```
sample output: 
```
baseline recall@10: 0.742
ptq6 recall@10: 0.674
delta: -0.068 (~9.2%)
```
Rafael: thanks. Two likely culprits: per-tensor quantization + zero-point bias, or a mismatch in the whitening pipeline prior to quant. Did you run the same L2 norm & PCA live transform?
Maya: yes preprocessing identical. I suspected bias from per-tensor scales. Ran a quick per-channel emulation on CPU and saw a ~3% recovery (ptq6-perchannel -> 0.707).
Priya: good signal. Can you try +calibration with 4k sample set (holdout from train) and asymmetric quant? Also try per-channel for the projection matrix only. Short queries are sensitive to small directional changes.
Maya: scheduling those runs now. Fast local patch: switched quant backend to per-channel for linear layers only and re-eval (local noisy run): recall@10: 0.709.
Jun: also try disabling range folding for the last projection (we saw similar issue with Hummingbird where fold reduced tail precision).
Rafael: FYI we should instrument top-k token distances distribution. If distances compress near zero after quant, knn rank ordering breaks. Could add a quick histogram in eval.
Maya: adding histograms. Example snippet I used: 
```python
# inside eval loop
dists = np.dot(query_vecs, db_vecs.T)  # cosine after norm
np.histogram(dists, bins=40)
```
Priya: another mitigation: run a small post-quant calibration linear layer (bias-correction) on the projection using 512 samples and re-eval. Cheap and often recovers directionality.
Maya: queued: per-channel PTQ + 4k calib asymmetric + bias-corr 512. ETA ~ 2h on staging.
ci-bot: test-run vector-sherpa ptq6-perchannel started on staging (run id: rs-2026-06-03-81).
Jun: please include recall@100 and MAP; short queries sometimes recover at higher k which affects product decisions.
Maya: will do. Quick note for release docs: mark vector_sherpa/ptq6 as "needs per-channel calibration" and don't set as default in canary until we validate.
Rafael: +1. After runs, if recovery <5% we can try INT4 mixed with residual FP for projection.
Priya: also add a small unit that compares whitening PCA components before/after quant to detect rotation drift.
Maya: plan: 1) per-channel PTQ run with 4k calib, 2) bias-corr 512, 3) histogram + PCA-drift check, 4) collect recall@10/@100 & MAP, 5) propose fallback policy for short queries (route to fp32 for k<=8). Will post results when done.
Jun: sounds good. Thanks Maya. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks, pinging @Rafael and @Priya for followups once runs finish.
